text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
IZVESTIA
- Russian recruits into the military continue living in prison-like conditions, says Amnesty International.
- President Yeltsin during his holiday break seems to be putting in more time working than resting.
- A new managing director at the giant Krasnoyarsk aluminium smelter (KrAZ) says he will not stay for long at the helm.
- Prominent international financier George Soros says he invested more than $980 million in Russian telecoms giant Svyazinvest.
- Separatist Chechen leaders have reacted strongly to Moscow's moves to alienate the rebel republic from major domestic communications lines.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Russia's banking community demonstrates its discontent over the results of the sell-off of Svyazinvest, the country's telecommunication giant.
- RAO Norilsky Nikel, on the eve of being auctioned, may face a bankruptcy case for non-payment for gas deliveries.
- Russian telecommunication companies' shares went up on the stock market after the Svyazinvest auction.
- Management of the KrAZ keeps changing and the situation around the smelter is very tense..
- George Soros wants to buy a stake in Rosneft, Russia's state-owned oil company which is to be privatised this year, and offers to pay for it $1 billion.

- President Boris Yeltsin's decree which puts all foreign contracts by Russia's main arms exporter, Rosvooruzheniye, under the direct control of Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, is the victory of the young reformers team.
SEVODNYA
- The newspaper attacks comments by First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov's on the "bandit capitalism" in Russia.
- Russia wants to regain its position as an exporter on the world grain market.
- There are all reasons to expect a heated battle for Rosneft.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The state budget lost about $2 billion because of the government mishandlin of Gazprom shares, the paper says.
- Signing an agreement with Azerbajan on the Kyapaz oil deposit in the Kaspian Sea was a blunder in the Russian foreign policy.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- Opinion polls show that both civilians and servicemen agree that the Russian army is in dire need of reform.
- Russia urgently needs proper tax reform, says former finance minister Boris Fyodorov.
- The Interior Ministry will soon have to hand over its prisons and camps to the Justice Ministry.
- Russian business tycoons use announcers at TV stations they control to present themselves as the voices of public opinion.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Moscow authorities have announced they will buy illegal firearms held by Muscovites at 'black market' prices.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin met Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais to work out how to put an end to the scandal sparked by the privatisation of telecoms giant Svyazinvest.
- Shares in Svyazinvest posted an unprecedented 10-14 percent rise within hours of the auction held to sell off a 25 percent stake in the company.
KOMSOMOLSKAYA PRAVDA
- A scandal around Svyazinvest is the first stage of the mass media warfare which accompanies privatisation.
PRAVDA-5
- Leaders of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan bring their positions closer together and farther distance themselves from Moscow.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
